flashcard_questions.a: The way people are spread across an area.

flashcard_questions.q: What share of the UK's population lives in urban areas?
Which UK region is the most densely populated?
flashcard_questions.a: The South East, especially Greater London.

flashcard_questions.q: Why are the Scottish Highlands so sparsely populated?
flashcard_questions.a: Harsh weather, thin soils and steep terrain leave few jobs.
The increase in the proportion of people living in towns and cities.

flashcard_questions.q: When did urbanisation begin in the UK?
flashcard_questions.a: During the Industrial Revolution of the late 18th century.
People moving from the countryside into towns and cities to find work.

flashcard_questions.q: Which river gave Liverpool its natural deep-water harbour?
What share of the world's trade did Liverpool handle by the early 20th century?
When did the Albert Dock open?
Which band formed in Liverpool in 1960?
What title did Liverpool hold in 2008?
How many universities are there in Liverpool and wider Merseyside?
How much cargo does the Port of Liverpool handle each year?
How much does tourism generate for Liverpool's economy each year?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term-to-definition (population distribution, urbanisation, rural-urban migration, densest region), 7 case-study-to-fact with one figure each (80% urban, 40% of world trade, Albert Dock 1846, 1960, 2008, 11 universities, £32 billion cargo, £5 billion tourism), 2 cause-to-consequence (Highlands sparsity, Mersey harbour), 2 place-to-feature. Dropped the '67 million visitors' figure because it would interfere with the UK's 67 million population, and left the Beatles' record sales out as flavour.
